attributes.probed_form: RETAINED, one probe, five sites (commit c6924cabb). Each of five consecutive guard PAIRS `if (A) { return; } if (B) { return; }` becomes one disjunctive guard `if (A || B) { return; }`: (1) `if (z1 <= (*(f32**)(win + 4))[22] || z1 >= (*(f32**)(win + 4))[23]) { return; }`; (2) `if (x1 < lbl_803451D4 || x1 >= lbl_803451D8) { return; }`; (3) `if (y1 < lbl_803451DC || y1 >= lbl_803451E0) { return; }`; (4) and (5) the identical two forms on x2 and y2. Result in that single probe: real 229 -> 194, insns O285 -> O290 against T290 (COUNT NOW EXACT), and the opcode multiset went from `target-only +5 b +5 bne / ours-only -5 beq` to IDENTICAL. MEASURED NEGATIVE on the surviving schedule residual: cache the draw counter across the volatile store block - add `s32 nq;`, write `nq = lbl_80345188 + 1;` immediately before the first `*(volatile f32*)0xCC008000 = ...` store and `lbl_80345188 = nq;` in place of the trailing `lbl_80345188 = lbl_80345188 + 1;`. real 194 -> 196, count and multiset unchanged. It DOES achieve the intended register separation (counter moves to r4, FIFO base stays r3) but overshoots the schedule - our `lwz` lands at +0x3f8, ahead of the `lis` base setup, where the target has it at +0x408 between the base setup and the first store - and it additionally front-loads five `lfs` stack reloads that the target interleaves among the stores, turning a compact two-atom displacement into a four-cluster scattered reorder. Reverted.
attributes.residual: real 194, insns T290/O290 EXACT, opcode multiset IDENTICAL - a pure reorder, SCHEDULE class, in one window at the GX FIFO store block. THE MECHANISM, named exactly: the target holds the FIFO base in r4 (`lis r4,-13311`, all twenty stores `stfs fN,-32768(r4)`) and the draw counter in r3, so it schedules `lwz r3,lbl_80345188` at +0x408 before the first store and `addi r0,r3,1` at +0x414 between the first and second store, keeping only `stw r0,lbl_80345188` at the end (+0x468). Ours holds the FIFO base in r3 and REUSES r3 for the counter, so all three counter instructions sit after the last store (+0x460 `lwz r3`, +0x464 `addi r0,r3,1`, +0x468 `stw r0`). NOT WEBFRANK-ELIGIBLE, and this is a guard result rather than a guess: the permutation that would fix it moves `lwz r3,lbl_80345188` from window position 22 to position 0, across roughly twenty `stfs fN,-32768(r3)` atoms that READ r3 as their base address. The moved atom WRITES r3. So the permutation is dependence-ILLEGAL in OUR colouring and the audit must fail closed on it, exactly as claim.law.C1_permute-recolor-composition-needs-a-permutation-legal-in-our-colouring.20260901.v1 requires - the atoms are independent in the TARGET's colouring only, which is not the test. Making it legal requires our base and counter to occupy different registers, which is a SOURCE problem, and the one source form that achieves the separation (the cached-counter probe above) buys it at the cost of a worse schedule. Reopen only with a lever over the placement of the stack reloads inside the volatile store block; do not re-probe the counter-caching axis or attempt a permutation rule against the current colouring.
